Đồng Chay, chân núi Ba Vì. Sương sớm còn: Đồng Chay, at the foot of Ba Vì mountain. Morning mist still clings to the tiled roofs. The students stop before the village gate, packs heavy, heads full of old legends.
Đủ cả rồi chứ? Hôm nay đi khảo sát, tối: Everyone here? We survey today, back to the guesthouse by night. If anyone feels tired, say so early. Don't push it.
Mệt gì mà mệt, mới tám giờ sáng! Tớ mang: Tired? It's eight in the morning! I brought a flashlight and spare batteries. Let me lead.
Đi đầu cái gì, hôm qua cậu còn sợ con ch: Lead, you? Yesterday you were scared of the guesthouse dog! ...Still, this village gate is beautiful. Hold still, let me get this shot first!
Hai người đừng đùa nữa... Bà tớ quê ở vù: You two, stop joking... My grandmother is from this area. She warned me carefully: in the forest, do not answer if someone calls your name. I mean it.
Tớ ghi lại hết. ...Nhưng cái tên “biệt t: I'm writing it all down. ...But the name “Vân Hòa villa” sounds terribly familiar. Yesterday I asked my grandmother, and she only went quiet and turned away.
Thế thì càng phải tìm hiểu cho ra nhẽ. N: Then we have all the more reason to get to the bottom of it. But one step at a time. First, let us ask the villagers.
Theo bản đồ thì đi qua ruộng, tới cây đa: The map says cross the fields to the banyan by the shrine, and that is the way into the forest. Still, we should ask again to be sure.

Ừ... Nhưng cậu để ý không? Hễ mình nhắc: Yes... But did you notice? The moment we mention the forest, everyone looks away. As if they fear that merely naming it will make it hear.
Ông cụ ngồi ở hiên nhà kia nhìn bọn mình: The old man on that veranda has been staring at us for a while. I waved, and he did not wave back. A little chilling.
Người già hay đề phòng người lạ thôi. Đi: Old people are wary of strangers, that is all. Let us move on. The light is still with us and we have much to do.
Qua cây cầu gỗ kia là tới lối vào rừng t: Past that wooden bridge is the way into the sacred forest. When I was small, my grandmother forbade me outright from going near it.
Cấm vì lý do gì thế? Cậu chưa kể bao giờ: Forbidden why? You have never told me.
Long ago the village carried offerings into the forest to pray for rain. After a year of famine, they stopped going in. My grandmother said only one thing: “The forest remembers what people wish to forget.”
Trời... nghe lạnh sống lưng. Cậu sờ thử: Heavens... that sends a chill down the spine. Feel it — I have gone all gooseflesh.
